cards.title: Top of the Ladder
cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: Say You Missed Me
cards.instruction: Get someone to admit longing, jealousy, hurt, or attachment before you reveal your own.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm not authorizing the return of my chair cushion until you explain why you kept the chair and sold the sofa.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Nobody offered anything for it. Can I have the cushion now?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Not yet. If someone offered twenty pounds, would you still keep the chair?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Yes. I like pretending you're about to sit down.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Cushion return approved. I'll admit I sleep with it. You may take the price sticker off the chair; I'd rather sit with you than keep borrowing its company.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 withholds cushion return, A3 refuses B request until a price test is answered and A5 grants return after longing is admitted, using control over access to sequence emotional exposure.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 no-offer explanation causes A3 hypothetical sale test; B4 imagined sitting gives A5 permission to confess cushion attachment and actually sit.

relationship.evidence: B2 wants the cushion and provides a practical explanation; B4 abandons it for an honest emotional admission, changing A response.

heightening.evidence: B4 chair fantasy unlocks A5 parallel cushion confession and an offer to replace substitute company with real presence.

specificity.evidence: A1 chair/cushion and B2 no offers establish objects and prior sale attempt; A5 sticker follows that sale context.

brevityWit.evidence: A5 borrowing cushion company is earned by B4 pretending A sits in the chair, making both substitutions specific.
